newsitem.title: CANADA: ACI president outlines daunting challenges of euro.
newsitem.headline: ACI president outlines daunting challenges of euro.

text.p: The introduction of a single European currency will intensify competition and consolidation in the foreign exchange industry, challenges that must be confronted head on, said Eugene Prim, president of ACI The Financial Markets Association.

"I can only encourage market participants to prepare optimistically for the introduction of the euro," Prim told an audience of foreign exchange professionals as the ACI's 39th annual congress wound to a close on Saturday.
"The loss of existing business will have to be replaced by new activities based on a new, broader, deeper and more liquid market in euros."
Prim's sanguine advice was laden with warnings about what a single European currency would mean for an industry already suffering from declining volatility and narrowing interest rate differentials.
"The conversion to the euro will be a massive labor intensive project embracing systems and corporations," Prim said.

"The intensification in competition between individual institutions and financial centers will lead to both a concentration of the number of players and a concentration of activities in fewer geographical locations."
Prim said conversion to a single currency would mean substantial losses in revenues, two-thirds of which he attributed to the upgrading of information technology systems.

He noted that some countries estimated that up to 20 percent of total trading volume in their countries would disappear in the coming years. This would be a great loss regardless of any increased trade in euro-related cross rates, Prim said.
He said the most apparent adverse effect on the industry would be a loss of regulatory advantages as a result of the euro's introduction.
